source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Apply a previously learned cultural profile to predict the patient’s preferences without asking about individual differences.","B":"Avoid discussing culture or bias so the nurse’s own values cannot influence the interaction.","C":"Treat completion of cultural-competence training as permanent mastery of the beliefs of patients from that group.","D":"Use ongoing self-reflection about bias, power, and assumptions while learning from the individual patient’s experiences, values, and preferences."}}
source_row.rationale: HHS's CLAS in Nursing program explicitly includes cultural humility and emphasizes self-awareness of beliefs and values as well as privilege, power, bias, and stereotypes, together with learning the patient's cultural identity and responding to the patient's experiences, values, beliefs, and preferences.
source_row.source_detail: Cultural humility includes self-awareness, attention to power and bias, and patient-centered learning Source has no separate formal version identifier in the cited page metadata; live currentness and applicability rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Psychosocial Integrity: mental-health symptom recognition, therapeutic communication, coping, cultural/spiritual influences and psychosocial support as applicable. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
